title: Embed/rerank surge: fallback analysis and scalability hardening
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket documents the operational incident on 2026-02-20 where the embeddings + reranking endpoints experienced a rapid capacity drop and quality regression during a traffic surge caused by a partner batch import. The event produced increased latencies (median token latency ~2x baseline), retry amplification, and a measurable drop in rerank precision for a subset of queries. This postmortem covers timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and planned follow-ups to harden scaling and fallback behavior.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-20T08:12 and 2026-02-20T12:45 UTC: capacity for embedding/rerank workers serving the eu-west region dropped to ~40% of expected due to GPU memory fragmentation + per-instance KV cache pressure. Median end-to-end rerank latency increased from 120ms to 270ms for p95, and customer-visible top-5 rerank precision fell by ~30% for the partner workload that used quantized model variants. Approximately 18% of requests hit the new fallback path (CPU or smaller model) and 4 customer integrations reported elevated error rates and timeouts in their dashboards.
timeline:
2026-02-20T08:12 UTC - Alert: autoscale controller shows failed scale-ups (OOMs).
2026-02-20T08:17 UTC - On-call triggered, initial hypothesis: misconfigured autoscale threshold.
2026-02-20T08:25 UTC - Observability: GPU free memory per pod is fragmented; large allocations fail despite aggregate free memory. KV cache eviction rate spiked; many hot prefixes thrashing.
2026-02-20T08:40 UTC - Rolled soft-fallback to smaller model variant for the partner (canary) which reduced memory pressure but lowered quality.
2026-02-20T09:10 UTC - Triggered rolling restarts of affected worker nodes to clear CUDA allocator fragmentation.
2026-02-20T09:40 UTC - Autoscaler policy temporarily increased target pool size and relaxed burst constraints.
2026-02-20T11:00 UTC - Latencies returned to within 1.2x baseline; error counts subsided.
2026-02-20T12:45 UTC - Incident declared resolved; continued monitoring through evening.
root_cause: Multiple contributing causes: (1) Model variant roll (silent change) introduced a new quantized kernel with larger ephemeral allocation patterns that increased fragmentation. (2) KV cache configuration for the rerank shard used a single global cache on each pod; during the partner's heavy batch import hot prefixes caused frequent large evictions and allocations. (3) The autoscaler logic rejected scale-ups because per-pod alloc failures were mistaken for sustained lack of demand (scale-down hysteresis bug). These combined led to effective capacity loss and forced fallbacks to lower-quality variants.
mitigations: Immediate actions during incident: (a) Temporarily pinned partner traffic to the non-quantized model variant for leaderboard queries. (b) Soft-fallback policy adjusted to prefer CPU-only small-model only after quota thresholds exceeded to avoid quality regressions. (c) Rolling restart of affected GPU nodes to reset CUDA allocator. (d) Autoscaler thresholds relaxed and a quick fix deployed to treat alloc failures as scale-up signal, not absence of demand.
remediation:
Post-incident fixes implemented in runtime-1.21: (1) Hotfix PR merged to autoscaler: treat per-pod OOM/alloc-failure signals as scale-up triggers (GH#1543). (2) KV cache sharding: introduced per-thread/fragmented caches and eviction backpressure (GH#1551). (3) Quantized kernel telemetry: added allocation histograms and preflight tests in CI to detect allocation pattern changes (GH#1562). (4) Added a capability to pin model variants per-customer during imports to avoid silent rollouts.
A full regression test matrix and a stress test harness were scheduled for Cycle 2026-W09 to exercise combined large-batch imports and concurrent rerank queries.
